comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a robot-axis damper through iterative adjustment and physical stop tests; pr-1906 performs an insulin-pen safety shot and sets a 12-unit dose.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key alignment, setscrew release, collar tuning, counterholding, relocking, and response-based correction. pr-1906 requires cap removal, needle-safe reorientation, short-stroke knob dialing with regrasping, axial injection force, and visual window correction.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable impact cycles, no bottoming or hard-stop strike, and post-lock setting retention. pr-1906 requires shield placement, an exact 2-unit dial and 5 s needle-up push to zero, then an exact 12-unit setting and safe released placement. Candidate rubric lacks numeric rebound, overload, collar-drift, and locking-torque limits.
comparison.reason: Rotary setting, regrasping, and visual/behavioral correction are shared primitives, but the candidate tests mechanical damping calibration and lock retention rather than a sequenced medication-device priming and dosing mechanism.
